spec.user_stories: - As the journal owner, I want GET /api/logs to return only the newest few logs by default, so the page does not slow down as the journal grows. - As an API client, I want an optional limit, so I can ask for more (up to a cap) or fewer logs. - As the journal owner, I want the server to read photo rows only for the logs it returns, so cost scales with the page size and not the journal size. - As an existing client, I want the response shape and ordering unchanged, so nothing else breaks.
spec.acceptance_criteria: 1. GET /api/logs with no query parameters, with more than 5 logs stored (e.g. 8), returns 200 and a JSON list of exactly 5 LogOut objects. 2. With fewer than 5 logs stored (0, 1, 3), GET /api/logs returns all of them (an empty list for 0). 3. GET /api/logs?limit=N for an integer N from 1 to 20 returns min(N, number of stored logs) logs (e.g. limit=2 with 8 stored returns 2; limit=8 with 8 stored returns 8). 4. GET /api/logs?limit=20 with 25 stored logs returns exactly 20. 5. A limit above 20 (e.g. 21, 100, 1000000) is clamped to 20: status 200, at most 20 logs, and with 25 stored logs exactly 20. It is not rejected. 6. A limit that is less than 1 (0, -1) or not an integer ("abc", "", "2.5") returns 422 with the API's usual error JSON. No logs are returned. 7. The returned logs are the newest ones, ordered created_at DESC, id DESC (ties on created_at: higher id first). With N logs stored and a limit L less than N, the response is exactly the first L of the full newest-first order, not an arbitrary subset. Checked with ids in creation order and with created_at set out of id order. 8. Each returned log carries exactly its own photos, in position then id order, with the same paths as when created. This holds for logs with 1 to 5 photos. A log that is not in the response never contributes photos to another log. 9. The photo query is restricted to the ids of the returned logs (WHERE log_id = ANY of those ids). Observable check: the response is correct when the table holds photos of non-returned logs, and no photo row of a non-returned log can appear in the output. When the log query returns no rows, the result is [] and the photo query is skipped or returns nothing. 10. Response format is unchanged: a bare JSON list of objects with exactly the fields id, description, photos, created_at, updated_at. There is no envelope, no total count, and no new response header required. 11. The default (5) and maximum (20) live as named constants in backend/models.py alongside the existing limits, and are used by both the route and the database function (no duplicated literals). 12. Existing behavior is untouched: POST, PUT and DELETE responses and status codes are unchanged. The 500 handling of GET /api/logs on a database error is unchanged. 13. New tests in backend/tests cover criteria 1, 3, 4/5 (over-max clamps to 20), 6, 7 and 8. They use TEST_DATABASE_URL and the temporary uploads folder only. The full existing suite passes, and any existing test that relied on listing more than 5 logs is adjusted without weakening what it asserts. 14. specs.md is updated: core feature 2 no longer says "all entries", and the GET /api/logs row and its notes document limit, default 5, max 20, clamping, the 422 on invalid values, and newest-first ordering. README.md is updated only if it describes the endpoint behavior (the grep shows only a file-structure line, so likely no change).
spec.assumptions: - limit below 1 or non-integer returns 422 (conventional, matches the API's other input errors). Planner's choice, not a user decision. - An absent limit and an explicit limit=5 behave identically. - Limit values with surrounding whitespace or "+5" follow whatever the framework's standard integer parsing does; they are not specified further. - Ordering stays created_at DESC, id DESC as in database.list_logs today. - No offset, paging cursor, or total count is added (CLAUDE.md: no new features). - The user's wording "Fetch photo records only for the logs included in the response" is met by filtering the photo query by log id, not by joining all photos.
spec.edge_cases: - Zero logs stored: [] with 200. - Exactly 5, exactly 20, and 21 logs stored with default and with limit=20. - limit=1. - Logs with identical created_at: the id tie-break decides which are cut off at the limit. - created_at out of id order: the newest by timestamp is kept, not the highest id. - Logs with several photos whose photo ids are not in position order: photos still ordered by position, then id. - Duplicate or repeated limit parameters (?limit=2&limit=3): framework default handling (last or first value); must not produce a 500. - Very large limit values (beyond 32-bit range) are clamped or rejected with 422, never a 500. - Deleting or editing a log then listing: the page shows the newest remaining logs up to the limit.

risks.risk: Known consequence, out of scope: frontend/app.js loads the list with a plain GET, so after this change the page shows only the newest 5 logs and older ones are not reachable in the UI (there is no paging). The user should decide on a follow-up (paging or "load more"). Do not add paging or change the frontend in this task.

Existing tests that count or compare full lists (test_database.py, test_logs.py, test_api.py, test_photos.py, test_validation.py:199) appear to use 5 or fewer logs, so they probably pass unchanged. The implementer must check the loop at test_validation.py:199 and any test that creates more than 5 logs.
Clamping instead of rejecting a value above 20 means a client cannot tell that its limit was reduced. That follows the user's "no more than 20" wording and the response has no envelope to report it.
Documented behavior changes (specs.md says all entries), so docs must change in step per CLAUDE.md.

spec.dependencies: - backend/database.py (list_logs), backend/routes.py (list_logs endpoint, _list), backend/models.py (new constants), specs.md, backend/tests/. - No new packages. FastAPI query-parameter handling and psycopg are already present. - A PostgreSQL database whose name ends in _test, supplied through TEST_DATABASE_URL.
spec.self_critique: Every story maps to a criterion: default and custom limit (1-5), newest-first (7), photos only for returned logs (8, 9), unchanged format (10, 12). Each criterion is observable through the HTTP response, except criterion 9's query restriction, which is only checkable by behavior, or by a test that spies on the SQL if the implementer wants it; the behavioral form is the required minimum. The biggest remaining uncertainty is the 422-versus-clamp choice for limit below 1, which the spec fixes at 422 (assumption), and the unreachable older logs in the UI, which the user must weigh.
